triggers.grounds: Two positional row references stand in the driver field boundary_rationale: 'The second-person address to God carried over from the preceding row resurfaces mid-strophe' and 'before an explanatory particle opens a fresh analogy in the next row'. E-18 arm re-derived from bytes: BOTH claims are TRUE - MT Job.13.20-Job.13.27 is sustained 2ms address to God (וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר at oshb:Job.13.27, a 2ms yiqtol pair), and MT Job.14.7 does open on the explanatory particle כִּ֤י (verse-initial, byte tier at oshb:Job.14.7); both edges are ref-anchored (web:Job.13.28 and web:Job.14.7 stand in boundary_evidence_refs). Only the register law is breached (row prose must describe the text, and cross-row reference must be verse-anchored, not positional), so this is a defect at low, cosmetic severity, not an evidence defect.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale carries two positional row references ('the preceding row', 'the next row') where the register law requires verse-anchored cross-row reference.
findings.grounds: Both phrases sit in the driver field. Their content is byte-true (2ms address across MT Job.13.20-Job.13.27; כִּ֤י verse-initial at oshb:Job.14.7), so this is register bleed only, with no effect on the seam at Job.13.28|Job.14.1, which rests on the fresh universal subject אָ֭דָם יְל֣וּד אִשָּׁ֑ה standing verse-initially in MT Job.14.1's own bytes (byte tier, sole book-wide hit).
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): re-word to verse-anchored form, e.g. 'the second-person address to God running through Job.13.20-Job.13.27 resurfaces mid-strophe' and 'before the explanatory particle at Job.14.7 opens a fresh analogy'.

findings.claim: 'Job.14.5 also carries a single-witness paseq elsewhere in the verse' asserts an intra-verse position the count-only paseq inventory cannot source, and the row's own next parenthetical concedes no position is encoded.
findings.grounds: pmarks_Job.json records paseq[Job.14.5] = 1 with paseq_note 'Seg layer, NOT quotable verse bytes; citable from this inventory only; COUNT-ONLY - intra-verse position claims are unsourceable'. 'elsewhere in the verse' is exactly such a position claim (it asserts the seg does not stand at the quoted words) and is contradicted three words later by the row's own '(inventory count alone, no word-level position encoded)'. The rest of the row's mark handling is CORRECT and is not part of this finding: kq[Job.14.5] = 1 and the staged extract does carry the ketiv+qere adjacent, חקו חֻקָּ֥יו, while the row's quoted Hebrew span חֻקָּ֥יו עָ֝שִׂ֗יתָ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר begins at the qere and does not cross the pair, and the K/Q is disclosed anyway.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): delete 'elsewhere in the verse' and keep the count-only disclosure, e.g. 'Job.14.5 also carries a single-witness paseq (inventory count alone, no word-level position encoded)'.

triggers.grounds: The matched phrase 'before the wish-formula that opens the next row' is a positional row reference in the driver field. E-18 arm re-derived from bytes: the claim is TRUE - MT Job.14.13 opens verse-initially on the wish formula מִ֤י יִתֵּ֨ן (byte tier at oshb:Job.14.13; the two-word idiom re-swept independently at skeleton tier = 10 tokens over 9 verses book-wide: Job.6.8, Job.11.5, Job.13.5, Job.14.4, Job.14.13, Job.19.23 x2, Job.23.3, Job.31.31, Job.31.35) - and web:Job.14.13 stands in boundary_evidence_refs. Register law breach only, therefore low and cosmetic.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale closes on a positional row reference ('the next row') where the register law requires verse-anchored cross-row reference.
findings.grounds: The referenced fact is byte-true at MT Job.14.13 (מִ֤י יִתֵּ֨ן, verse-initial, byte tier) and web:Job.14.13 is in refs; the defect is register only and touches no warrant.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'before the wish-formula at Job.14.13'.

findings.claim: The '44 verses' digit is attached to the wrong count object: it is the count of the meteg-LESS CLASS, not of 'the form this verse's own opening carries', which is verse-initial in 26 verses.
findings.grounds: Re-swept independently over the first word of every verse in verse_map_oshb.json: verse-initial ki at skeleton tier = 82 verses (the row's 82 is exact); of these the meteg-bearing form is verse-initial in 38 verses (the row's 38 is exact) and the meteg-less remainder in 44 verses (the row's 44 is exact for that CLASS). But the meteg-less remainder spans five distinct pointings, and the exact byte form MT Job.14.7 itself opens with, כִּ֤י, is verse-initial in only 26 verses. The row's phrase 'the meteg-less form this verse's own opening carries' names a single form and then carries the class digit. Nothing load-bearing turns on it: the claim is a dampener (verse-initial ki 'cannot alone carry a boundary'), which 26, 44 and 82 support equally.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): name the object, e.g. '82 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, of which 38 open on the meteg-bearing form and 44 on meteg-less pointings (26 of them on the exact form this verse opens with)'.

findings.claim: Two Hebrew splices over-run their English glosses: the closing splice carries one word the gloss does not render, and the opening splice carries the particle the gloss drops.
findings.grounds: Closing splice עַד בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ וְלֹֽא is byte-exact at oshb:Job.14.12, but its gloss 'Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake' renders only through יָקִ֑יצוּ; the trailing וְלֹֽא is unglossed (WEB Job.14.12 continues 'nor be roused out of their sleep.'). Opening splice כִּ֤י יֵ֥שׁ לָעֵ֗ץ תִּ֫קְוָ֥ה אִֽם יִ֭כָּרֵת is byte-exact at oshb:Job.14.7, but its gloss 'there is hope for a tree if it is cut down' drops WEB Job.14.7's own leading 'For', which renders כִּ֤י. Both curly-quoted English runs are themselves verbatim WEB - check_web_quotes.py over a private copy of the seven shipped rows returned 23 quotes checked, 0 flags, 0 neighbor-only warns - so this is extent parity only.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): trim the closing splice to עַד בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ (oshb:Job.14.12), or extend the gloss to WEB's 'they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep'; and quote WEB's 'For there is hope for a tree if it is cut down' to match the spliced particle.

triggers.grounds: Calibration is sound at medium_low. The seam at Job.16.14|Job.16.15 is a real participant-role shift standing in the cited verse's own bytes: MT Job.16.15 opens שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי (fronted object plus 1cs qatal) and continues 1cs at וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי, against MT Job.16.9-Job.16.14 where the assailant is subject and Job the object (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי at oshb:Job.16.9). But the seam carries no formula, no vocative and no parashah mark (pmarks_Job.json records no PE/SAMEKH anywhere in ch 16 - absence is never counterevidence, only the absence of corroboration), and the role contrast is not clean, since MT Job.16.12 already opens on a 1cs subject clause שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי inside the preceding row. The row itself concedes the softness ('word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge'). No Job cap is implicated: this is a 3-verse in-speech strophe row, not a whole chapter. Confidence is neither over- nor under-stated.

Two positional row references in the driver field, and the first carries a byte-FALSE claim about another row, so the E-18 arm applies and the disposition is medium, not cosmetic. 'The preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, ... Job.16.12)': the preceding row M8-Job-063 spans Job.16.9-Job.16.14, so its OPENING verse is Job.16.9, whose own first words are אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף (subject before verb); שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי (byte tier at oshb:Job.16.12) stands at the FOURTH verse of that row. The second reference ('a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row') is TRUE - MT Job.16.18 opens on the vocative אֶ֭רֶץ - but is anchored to no ref at all: neither web:Job.16.18 nor oshb:Job.16.18 appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The row mislocates its cross-row comparison: Job.16.12 is the fourth verse of the preceding row, not that row's opening.
findings.grounds: Shipped prev row M8-Job-063 span = Job.16.9-Job.16.14. Its opening verse MT Job.16.9 begins אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף - itself a subject fronted before its verb - so the comparison the row wants is available at the true opening and the underlying point (fronting is ambient here, hence non-distinctive as an edge signal) survives. What is false is only the locator: שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי is byte-exact at oshb:Job.16.12 (byte tier, sole book-wide hit) and Job.16.12 is verse four of the preceding row's six. The same verse also softens the row's other contrast, between 'the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14)' and 'the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts': הָיִ֨יתִי at oshb:Job.16.12 is itself a 1cs qatal inside the range said to hold Job as object.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): re-word to 'the preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it', and add oshb:Job.16.9 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: Positional row references in the driver field, one of them carrying a true far-edge fact with no supporting ref.
findings.grounds: 'The preceding row' and 'the next row' are positional rather than verse-anchored. The far-edge fact is byte-true - MT Job.16.18 opens on the vocative אֶ֭רֶץ (byte tier at oshb:Job.16.18) - but boundary_evidence_refs lists only web:Job.16.15, web:Job.16.16, web:Job.16.17, oshb:Job.16.15, oshb:Job.16.12 and the five single-verse web: refs for Job.16.9-Job.16.14, with no Job.16.18 ref in either space.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): verse-anchor both references and add web:Job.16.18 (or oshb:Job.16.18) to boundary_evidence_refs.

triggers.grounds: medium_low is the honest label for this row's own evidence and is neither over- nor under-stated in a way that changes the span. Far edge: MT Job.17.10 opens וְֽאוּלָ֗ם כֻּלָּ֣ם תָּ֭שֻׁבוּ וּבֹ֣אוּ - an adversative followed by 2mp imperatives, a genuine tier-1 address shift back to the friends, exactly as the row says ('the direct address to the friends that reopens at 17:10'). Near edge: MT Job.17.6 opens on the waw-continuation וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי (waw plus 3ms hiphil plus 1cs suffix) - no formula, no vocative, no interrogative - and pmarks_Job.json records no PE/SAMEKH anywhere in Job.17.1-Job.17.15 (the chapter's single mark is the SAMEKH after Job.17.16; absence is never counterevidence). A row whose far edge carries a formula-grade signal and whose opening does not is correctly held below medium. The separate warrant and field shortfalls recorded below do not make the confidence label itself wrong.

findings.claim: The opening seam is argued from topic alone; the driver field cites no original-language evidence and does not use the participant/address shift that actually stands at Job.17.5|Job.17.6.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale contains zero Hebrew runs and all six boundary_evidence_refs are web: refs (the row carries no oshb: ref at all), so no seam warrant rests on bytes in the cited verse. The available signal is unclaimed: MT Job.17.4 is 2ms address to God (צָפַ֣נְתָּ and תְרֹמֵֽם, both 2ms), Job.17.5 is a third-person maxim, and MT Job.17.6 opens וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי, turning to a 3ms subject acting on a 1cs object - the address/participant shift the owner-ruled strategy's section 6 lists among the tier-1 seam signals. The row instead offers only 'a distinct topic'. The seam is defensible on the bytes; the warrant as written is not byte-grounded.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): add the 2ms-to-3ms address shift with the verse-initial וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי, citing oshb:Job.17.4 and oshb:Job.17.6, and add those oshb: refs to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: literature_type_guess names an orphaning motif that does not stand anywhere in the row's span.
findings.grounds: literature_type_guess = 'Contempt-from-humans catalog with complete orphaning state'. Swept over verse_map_oshb.json at skeleton tier, the orphan lexeme (the plene form spliced from oshb:Job.24.9) occurs book-wide at MT Job.6.27, Job.22.9 (defective plural יְתֹמִ֣ים), Job.24.9 (plene singular יָת֑וֹם), Job.29.12, Job.31.17 and Job.31.21 - none of them inside Job.17.6-Job.17.9, whose four verses carry no orphan, widow or bereavement lexeme at all. The 'catalog' half is also only half true: WEB Job.17.8-Job.17.9 is a righteous-response maxim, which the row's own prose calls 'a maxim of perseverance', not contempt from humans.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): restate literature_type_guess from the span's own content, e.g. 'public-shame complaint closing on a righteousness maxim'.

triggers.grounds: The matched clause - 'the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token' - is a translation-punctuation fact sitting in the driver field with no tier-4 disclosure, and it carries argumentative weight: it amplifies the interrogative-density characterization of Job.22.2-Job.22.5 on which the far-edge rejection at Job.22.5|Job.22.6 leans. It is factually TRUE (WEB Job.22.2 carries one question mark, WEB Job.22.3 two, WEB Job.22.4 one = four question-marked clauses out of the first three he-tokens; the second colon does open mid-verse on וְאִם), and web:Job.22.2, web:Job.22.3, web:Job.22.4 stand in boundary_evidence_refs. Under the campaign-wide addendum WEB punctuation is tier-4 and is never boundary evidence, so the corroborative use is a defect; severity is LOW because it is a stray remark inside an otherwise byte-grounded case - the opening seam rests on the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.22.1 and the far-edge rejection rests separately on the Hebrew הֲלֹ֣א cited as oshb:Job.22.5 and on the connectives of Job.22.6, Job.22.8 and Job.22.11.

'the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1)' is a positional row reference AND is byte-false about that row, so the E-18 arm applies at medium: shipped prev row M8-Job-088 spans Job.21.27-Job.21.34 and closes at Job.21.34 (pmarks_Job.json: marks[Job.21.34] = SAMEKH, which that row itself cites), so וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at MT Job.21.1 is the previous SPEECH's opening formula, not the previous ROW's close. The same sentence also mis-notates the seam as 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1', pairing two verses 34 apart in the corpus's own adjacent-verse pipe notation; the actual seam is Job.21.34|Job.22.1.

findings.claim: The opening-seam sentence mis-notates the seam (Job.21.1|Job.22.1 for Job.21.34|Job.22.1) and mis-describes the previous row as closing with the vaya'an of Job.21.1.
findings.grounds: Prev row M8-Job-088 span = Job.21.27-Job.21.34; MT Job.21.1 (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, byte tier, one of the nine book-wide members of the generic Job-reply formula) sits 26 verses before that row's first verse and opens Job's speech, not any row's close. The corpus uses X|Y for ADJACENT verses - this same slice writes 'Job.22.25|Job.22.26' and 'Job.22.24|Job.22.25' - so 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1' is a wrong-seam cite. The seam itself is unaffected and correct: MT Job.22.1 carries the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (byte tier at oshb:Job.22.1, sole book-wide hit), and the prev row independently corroborates its own close with the SAMEKH after Job.21.34.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34, and this row opens with Eliphaz answering, וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.22.1)'.

findings.claim: 'Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12' is byte-false as to 'final': a sixth verse-initial interrogative he opens Job.22.15.
findings.grounds: Re-swept over the first word of every verse of Eliphaz's third speech (MT Job.22.2-Job.22.30) in verse_map_oshb.json. Verse-initial interrogative he: Job.22.2 הַלְאֵ֥ל, Job.22.3 הַחֵ֣פֶץ, Job.22.4 הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ, Job.22.5 הֲלֹ֣א, Job.22.12 הֲֽלֹא and Job.22.15 הַאֹ֣רַח - six members, so Job.22.12 is correctly the FIFTH but is not the final one. WEB Job.22.15 confirms the interrogative reading ('Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,'), the question running on into Job.22.16 so that no question mark falls inside Job.22.15 itself. The two near-miss verse-initial he-tokens are correctly excluded from the series: Job.22.17's הָאֹמְרִ֣ים is the qamats-he ARTICLE on a participle and Job.22.21's הַסְכֶּן is a hiphil imperative. Not load-bearing - the claim sits beyond the row's far edge and neither the seam nor the rival's rejection rests on it. (The row's other digits in this field re-derive TRUE: the defective Temanite spelling sweeps 1 book-wide, at Job.22.1 alone, and the fuller spelling 5 book-wide at Job.2.11, Job.4.1, Job.15.1, Job.42.7 and Job.42.9, exactly the members listed - a spelling-level, not byte-level, object, the pointed form הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י at oshb:Job.22.1 being a byte singleton and הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י standing byte-identically at oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1 only.)
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative falls outside this row at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15).'

findings.claim: A WEB-punctuation observation does corroborative work in the driver field with no tier-4 disclosure.
findings.grounds: See the punct trigger disposition: the claim is true (four question marks across WEB Job.22.2-Job.22.4, with Job.22.3's second colon וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ rendered as a question) but WEB punctuation is tier-4 under the campaign addendum and is never boundary evidence; here it is offered as an amplification of the question-series characterization rather than flagged as metadata, and a disclosure would not cure it if it were driving. Low, because the seam (וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.22.1) and the rival's rejection (the Hebrew הֲלֹ֣א at oshb:Job.22.5) are byte-grounded independently of it.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): delete the punctuation clause, or mark it explicitly as tier-4 metadata carrying no evidential weight.

findings.claim: 'three of the catalogue's six verses ... open on overt connectives ... rather than asyndetically' undercounts: four of the six do, so the implied asyndeton of Job.22.10 is false.
findings.grounds: MT first words of the catalogue Job.22.6-Job.22.11: Job.22.6 כִּֽי, Job.22.7 לֹא, Job.22.8 וְאִ֣ישׁ, Job.22.9 אַ֭לְמָנוֹת, Job.22.10 עַל כֵּ֭ן, Job.22.11 אוֹ. The row names three (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.11), but Job.22.10 also opens on an overt connective - the adjacent shipped row M8-Job-090 itself calls עַל כֵּ֭ן 'an explicit consequence particle' (oshb:Job.22.10) - leaving only Job.22.7 and Job.22.9 asyndetic. Each of the three named members is individually true and the direction of the error strengthens rather than weakens the row's own register-contrast point, so this is a completeness / count-object shortfall, not a defective warrant.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'four of the catalogue's six verses (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.10, Job.22.11) open on overt connectives'.

triggers.grounds: Two positional row references in the driver field. E-18 arm re-derived from bytes: BOTH claims are TRUE. The imperative-to-promise register shift does fall at Job.22.24|Job.22.25 - MT Job.22.24 opens on the imperative וְשִׁית and MT Job.22.25 on the waw-qatal consequent וְהָיָ֣ה - inside the preceding row M8-Job-092, whose span is exactly Job.22.21-Job.22.25 as the row states; and Job's own vaya'an does open the next row, MT Job.23.1 = וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר (byte tier at oshb:Job.23.1). Register law breach only, therefore low; note additionally that the Job.23.1 fact carries no ref - neither oshb:Job.23.1 nor web:Job.23.1 appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: By the row's own byte analysis its opening seam at Job.22.25|Job.22.26 carries no signal of any tier, and the sole ground offered for retaining it - preserving the petuchah's association with Job.22.30 - is a non-sequitur.
findings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes: MT Job.22.23 opens the protasis אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב, Job.22.24 continues on the imperative וְשִׁית, Job.22.25 is the waw-qatal consequent וְהָיָ֣ה, and Job.22.26 opens כִּי אָ֭ז - a continuation particle inside that same result chain, exactly as the row itself states ('no renewed protasis, address-shift, or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself'). All of Job.22.21-Job.22.30 is one unbroken 2ms address with no vocative, no speech formula and no parashah mark until the PE that pmarks_Job.json records after Job.22.30 (marks[Job.22.30] = PE - petuchah, single-witness, Writings tier-3 weak corroboration only; the row's mark type and cite form are correct). The row's second retention ground is placed by the row itself one verse earlier, inside the preceding row (וְשִׁית at oshb:Job.22.24 to וְהָיָ֣ה at oshb:Job.22.25), so it cannot mark this row's opening. The petuchah ground does not follow: a merged Job.22.21-Job.22.30 row would still close at Job.22.30, where the petuchah stands, so merging erases nothing. Job's owner-ruled strategy section 6 seams rows at tier-1 signals ONLY, and the confidence label 'medium' is over-stated for a seam the row concedes is unmarked.
